body: Current LLM safety benchmarks largely rely on binary metrics, overlooking how models respond to harmful prompts with varying threat implicitness. We introduce TIER, a Threat Implicitness Benchmark for behavioral safety evaluation of LLMs. TIER covers four risk domains and four threat levels, from explicit harmful requests to sophisticated jailbreaks. Responses are assessed using a six-label behavior scale and two independent LLM judges. Experiments on six open-weight LLMs show that safety behaviors evolve gradually across threat levels rather than shifting directly from refusal to compliance. Contextual prompts yield the most diverse behaviors, while jailbreaks reveal the largest robustness gaps. Furthermore, models with similar Attack Success Rates can exhibit distinct response distributions, highlighting the need for behavior-aware LLM safety evaluation.
summaryZh: 该研究引入了TIER（Threat Implicitness Benchmark），一个用于评估大型语言模型（LLM）安全行为的新基准。TIER超越了现有基准的二元指标，通过考虑从明确的有害请求到复杂的越狱提示等不同威胁隐晦程度，并使用六标签行为尺度和两个独立的LLM裁判来评估模型响应。实验表明，LLM的安全行为随威胁程度的增加而逐渐演变，而非直接从拒绝转变为合规。研究强调了行为感知LLM安全评估的必要性，因为具有相似攻击成功率的模型可能表现出不同的响应分布。
